title: Climbing Stairs
statement: You are climbing a staircase that has n steps. Each move, you can climb either 1 step or 2 steps. Given an integer n (0 <= n <= 45), return the number of distinct ways you can climb to the top. n = 0 counts as exactly one way (you are already at the top, so there is one 'empty' sequence of moves).
hints: Think about the last move you make: it is either a single step from n-1, or a double step from n-2.
The number of ways to reach step n is the sum of the ways to reach step n-1 and step n-2 — this is a 1-D recurrence with only two prior states needed.
Keep two running variables prev2, prev1 for ways(n-2) and ways(n-1); iterate from 2 to n updating prev2, prev1 = prev1, prev2 + prev1, and handle n <= 1 as a base case returning 1.
